title: ActualSurface
description: What a codebase REALLY exposes, in manifest vocabulary. Produced by a per-stack adapter (Rust: syn; JVM: annotation scan; Node: router table), consumed by `rqunit conformance`, which owns the diff against the manifest. Adapters extract and never judge: no adapter decides what a divergence means.

generated_by.description: Adapter name and version — the report attributes findings to their extractor.

services.description: Keyed by manifest service slug. A service absent here is not reconciled at all (no adapter covers it); a service present with empty surfaces asserts the code exposes nothing.

access.description: Structural access tier as the code composes it (which middleware stack the route is mounted under). Membership in access_tiers is the manifest's business, not the adapter's.

direction.description: Optional: adapters that cannot determine direction omit it, and the reconciler falls back to presence-only matching.

covers.description: Which surface families this artifact EXAMINED. A probe reads one framework and finds one family, so an artifact from a NATS probe makes no claim about routes — and without this key the reconciler reads that silence as 'the code serves no endpoints' and reports every declared route as unserved. Omit to mean 'everything', which is what a single whole-stack extractor asserts and what every pre-existing artifact meant.

observed_shape.description: What the code DECLARES it carries in this direction — the handler's request or response type and that type's field names. Optional at every level: an adapter that cannot resolve a handler to a type omits the block, and one that can name the type but not walk its fields omits `fields`. Omission means 'not observed', never 'empty' — so a stack whose extractor cannot see shapes degrades to presence-only matching rather than reporting every declared field as missing.

type_name.description: The declared type, e.g. 'MeResponse'. Identity only: the reconciler uses it to notice that two routes serve the SAME type while their manifests declare different censuses (CF8). The adapter does not decide whether that is wrong.

fields.description: Field names the type declares, dotted for nesting, in manifest vocabulary. Names only: whether a field is required, nullable, or must not leak is a runtime and requirement question the manifest answers and tests prove — an adapter reporting it would be judging.
